questions.questionText: Choose the correct word: 'The ____ is shining brightly today. It's a perfect day for the beach.'
questions.explanation: 'Sun' is the correct word. 'Sun is shining' = bright daylight. Other options (moon/cloud/star) don't fit the beach context.

questions.questionText: Which sport uses a racket to hit a ball over a net?
questions.explanation: Tennis uses a racket. Football uses a ball with feet. Swimming is in water. Cycling is on a bike.

questions.questionText: Which subject involves studying about chemical reactions and the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Chemistry is the subject that studies chemical reactions and the periodic table.

questions.questionText: A person who treats sick animals is called a:
questions.explanation: Veterinarian = animal doctor. Doctor/nurse treat humans. Dentist treats teeth.

questions.questionText: What is the opposite of 'ancient'?
questions.explanation: 'Modern' is opposite of 'ancient'. 'Ancient' = very old. 'Modern' = new/current.

questions.questionText: Choose the action verb: 'She ___ to the radio every morning.'
questions.explanation: 'Listens' is the action verb. 'Quickly' is an adverb. 'Blue' is an adjective. 'Happiness' is a noun.

questions.questionText: What does 'enormous' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Enormous' means 'very big/huge'. Synonym: gigantic, massive.

questions.questionText: What is the opposite of 'generous'?
questions.explanation: 'Stingy' is opposite of 'generous'. 'Generous' = willing to give. 'Stingy' = unwilling to share.

questions.questionText: What do we call the day before yesterday?
questions.explanation: Day before yesterday = two days ago. 'Today' = now. 'Tomorrow' = next day. 'Last week' = 7+ days ago.

questions.questionText: What does the prefix 'un-' mean in the word 'unhappy'?
questions.explanation: Prefix 'un-' means 'not'. 'Unhappy' = not happy. Other prefixes: 're-' = again, 'pre-' = before, 'very' has no prefix.

questions.questionText: What type of word is 'celebration'?
questions.explanation: Suffix '-tion' makes nouns from verbs. 'Celebrate' (verb) → 'celebration' (noun).

questions.questionText: What does 'look after' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Look after' = take care of. 'I look after my little brother' = I take care of him.

questions.questionText: What does 'give up' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Give up' = stop trying. 'Don't give up' = don't stop trying.

questions.questionText: What is a 'rainbow'?

options.label: B
options.text: An arc of colours in the sky after rain

questions.explanation: 'Rainbow' = 'rain' + 'bow'. An arc of colours appearing in the sky after rain.

questions.questionText: Which word is a synonym for 'happy'?
questions.explanation: 'Joyful' = full of joy = happy. Synonym (same meaning).

questions.questionText: What is the antonym (opposite) of 'optimistic'?
questions.explanation: 'Pessimistic' = opposite of 'optimistic'. 'Optimistic' = hopeful. 'Pessimistic' = expecting bad outcomes.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct meaning: 'She went to the bank to deposit money.'
questions.explanation: Context 'deposit money' indicates 'financial institution'. 'Bank' has multiple meanings (polysemy).

questions.questionText: Choose the best word: 'Despite the rain, the match continued. The players were ____ to play in wet conditions.'
questions.explanation: Context 'despite rain, continued' implies they were 'willing' to play in wet conditions. 'Unable' contradicts 'continued'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct past tense: 'Yesterday, she ___ to the market.'
questions.explanation: 'Went' is past tense of 'go' (irregular verb). 'Go' = present, 'goes' = present 3rd person, 'going' = present participle.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: 'They ___ football yesterday afternoon.'
questions.explanation: 'Played' = past tense (regular verb: play + ed). 'Plays' = present 3rd person. 'Playing' = present participle.

questions.questionText: Identify the grammatically correct sentence about future action:

options.label: A
options.text: I will goes to school tomorrow.

options.label: B
options.text: I will go to school tomorrow.

options.label: C
options.text: I will going to school tomorrow.

options.label: D
options.text: I will gone to school tomorrow.

questions.explanation: After 'will' use base form of verb (go). 'Will goes', 'will going', 'will gone' are all grammatically incorrect.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: 'Look at those clouds! It ___ rain soon.'
questions.explanation: 'Be going to' for planned/predicted future. Correct form: 'It is going to rain'.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a grammatically correct present perfect sentence?

options.label: A
options.text: I have visited Paris last year.

options.label: B
options.text: I have visited Paris three times.

questions.explanation: Present perfect (have/has + past participle) for experiences. 'Last year' needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: 'By the time I arrived, the bus ___.'
questions.explanation: Past perfect (had + past participle) for actions completed before another past action.

questions.questionText: Pick the sentence that correctly uses past continuous tense:

options.label: A
options.text: I was reading a book when the phone rang.

options.label: B
options.text: I am reading a book when the phone rang.

options.label: C
options.text: I were reading a book when the phone rang.

options.label: D
options.text: I read a book when the phone was ringing.

questions.explanation: Past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) for ongoing action in past interrupted by another past action.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the modal verb 'should'?
questions.explanation: After modal verb 'should' use base form (study). Not 'to study', not '-ing', not past tense.

questions.questionText: Identify the sentence that correctly uses 'must':

options.label: A
options.text: You must to wear a helmet.

questions.explanation: After modal verb 'must' use base form (wear).

questions.questionText: Choose the correct meaning: 'It might rain tomorrow.'

options.label: B
options.text: It is possible to rain (small chance).

questions.explanation: 'Might' expresses possibility (small chance). Compare 'will' (certain), 'might' (possible), 'must' (obligation/strong likelihood).

questions.questionText: Choose the correct first conditional sentence:

options.label: A
options.text: If it rains, I will stay home.

options.label: B
options.text: If it rain, I will stay home.

options.label: C
options.text: If it rained, I will stay home.

options.label: D
options.text: If it rains, I would stay home.

questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb. 'If it rains, I will stay home.'

questions.questionText: Choose the correct second conditional:

options.label: A
options.text: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.

options.label: B
options.text: If I win the lottery, I would travel the world.

options.label: C
options.text: If I have won the lottery, I would travel the world.

options.label: D
options.text: If I will win the lottery, I travel the world.

questions.explanation: Second conditional (unreal/hypothetical): If + past simple, would + base verb.

questions.questionText: Identify the passive voice: 'The cake was eaten by the children.'
questions.explanation: Passive voice: subject receives action. Form: be + past participle ('was eaten').

questions.questionText: Convert to passive: 'The chef cooked the meal.'

options.label: B
options.text: The meal is cooked by the chef.

options.label: C
options.text: The meal cooked by the chef.

options.label: D
options.text: The meal was cooking by the chef.

questions.explanation: Passive: subject (meal) + be + past participle + by agent. 'The meal is cooked by the chef.'

questions.questionText: Convert to reported speech: 'I am happy,' she said.

options.label: A
options.text: She said that I am happy.

options.label: B
options.text: She said that she was happy.

options.label: C
options.text: She said that she is happy.

questions.explanation: Reported speech: present simple (am) shifts to past simple (was). Pronoun shifts (I → she).

questions.questionText: Convert to reported speech: 'Where do you live?' he asked.

options.label: A
options.text: He asked where do I live.

questions.explanation: Reported question: statement form (no do/does), tense shift (live → lived). 'He asked where I lived.'

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the relative pronoun 'who' correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: The man who lives next door is a doctor.

options.label: B
options.text: The man which lives next door is a doctor.

options.label: C
options.text: The man whose lives next door is a doctor.

options.label: D
options.text: The man where lives next door is a doctor.

questions.explanation: 'Who' = relative pronoun for people. 'Which' = things. 'Whose' = possession. 'Where' = places.

questions.questionText: Select the sentence that correctly uses 'which' for things:

options.label: A
options.text: The book who I bought is interesting.

options.label: B
options.text: The book which I bought is interesting.

options.label: C
options.text: The book whose I bought is interesting.

options.label: D
options.text: The book where I bought is interesting.

questions.explanation: 'Which' = relative pronoun for things. 'Who' = people.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: 'She enjoys ___ to classical music.'
questions.explanation: After 'enjoy' use gerund (-ing form). 'Enjoy listening' (not 'enjoy to listen').

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: 'I want ___ a doctor.'
questions.explanation: After 'want' use infinitive with 'to'. 'I want to be' (not 'want be' or 'want being').

questions.questionText: Choose the correct question tag: 'You are a student, ___?'
questions.explanation: Negative tag after positive statement: 'You are...aren't you?' (positive → negative tag).

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the article correctly?
questions.explanation: When 'school' refers to its primary function (as a student), no article is used. 'I went to school' = I attended school as a student.

questions.questionText:
Read:

Siti woke up early every morning to help her mother in the kitchen. She learned to cook traditional dishes and loved trying new recipes. By the time she was twelve, she could cook meals for the whole family.

What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: B
options.text: Siti learned to cook at a young age.

questions.explanation: Main idea: Siti learned to cook from a young age and could cook for the family by 12.

questions.questionText:
Read:

First, Ahmad turned on the computer. Then he opened the document. After that, he started typing his essay. Finally, he saved the file.

What did Ahmad do FIRST?
questions.explanation: FIRST action: 'First, Ahmad turned on the computer.'

questions.questionText:
Read:

The roads were flooded after the heavy rain. Many cars could not pass through the streets.

Why were the roads flooded?
questions.explanation: Cause: 'after the heavy rain'. Effect: roads flooded.

questions.questionText:
Read:

Ahmad looked at the clock. It was already 8 PM. He quickly gathered his books and ran out the door.

Where was Ahmad probably going?
questions.explanation: Ahmad 'ran out the door' at 8 PM after gathering books = probably late for school/class.

questions.questionText:
Read:

Despite being the smallest boy in class, Ali always stood up to bullies. He protected his friends and never ran away from trouble.

How would you describe Ali?
questions.explanation: Ali 'stood up to bullies' and 'never ran away' = brave/courageous.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The sun was setting behind the mountains. Birds were flying home to their nests. The villagers lit their lanterns as darkness approached.

When did this story take place?
questions.explanation: Clues: 'sun setting', 'birds flying home', 'villagers lit lanterns', 'darkness approached' = evening.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The children were famished after the long hike. They sat down and ate their sandwiches quickly.

What does 'famished' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Famished' = extremely hungry. Clue: 'ate sandwiches quickly'.

questions.questionText:
Read:

Fatimah is a librarian. She works at the school library every day from 8 AM to 4 PM. She helps students find books and keeps the library organized.

Where does Fatimah work?
questions.explanation: Specifically mentioned: 'school library'.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The lush green forest was home to many creatures. Tall trees reached up to the bright blue sky. A small stream flowed gently through the rocks.

Which word describes the forest?
questions.explanation: Direct quote: 'The lush green forest'.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The old wooden house stood at the edge of the cliff, overlooking the deep blue ocean. Wild flowers grew in the garden.

Where is the house located?

options.label: B
options.text: At the edge of a cliff

questions.explanation: Direct quote: 'stood at the edge of the cliff'.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The sweet smell of jasmine filled the air. The flowers glistened with morning dew. A gentle breeze rustled the leaves.

Which sense does 'sweet smell' appeal to?
questions.explanation: 'Sweet smell' appeals to sense of smell.

questions.questionText:
Read:

Dark clouds gathered overhead. The wind howled through the empty streets. Thunder rumbled in the distance.

What is the atmosphere like?
questions.explanation: Words: 'dark clouds', 'howled', 'rumbled' = ominous, impending storm.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The young girl's face was pale. Her hands trembled as she held the letter. Tears rolled down her cheeks.

How was the girl feeling?
questions.explanation: Clues: 'pale face', 'trembling hands', 'tears' = sad, distressed.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The new building was as tall as a mountain. Its windows gleamed like diamonds in the sunlight.

What is being compared to a mountain?
questions.explanation: 'The new building was as tall as a mountain' = building compared to mountain.

questions.questionText:
Read:

First, boil the water. Then, add the tea leaves. Next, pour the tea into a cup. Finally, add sugar to taste.

What should you do FIRST when making tea?
questions.explanation: First step: 'boil the water'.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The library is open Monday to Friday from 9 AM to 6 PM. On Saturday, it closes at 1 PM. The library is closed on Sundays.

On which day is the library closed?
questions.explanation: Direct quote: 'closed on Sundays'.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The recipe says: 'Mix flour, sugar, and eggs. Bake at 180°C for 30 minutes.'

What is the purpose of this text?
questions.explanation: 'Recipe' + 'mix' + 'bake' = procedural text giving instructions.

questions.questionText:
Read:

GRAND SALE! 50% off all items this weekend only. Don't miss out!

What is the purpose of this text?
questions.explanation: Words like 'SALE', '50% off', 'Don't miss out!' = persuasive advertisement.

questions.questionText:
Read:

A: 'Excuse me, could you tell me the way to the post office?'
B: 'Go straight for two blocks, then turn left. It's on your right.'

What does person B do?
questions.explanation: Person B provides directions to the post office.

questions.questionText:
Read:

A: 'Would you like some tea?'
B: 'I'd love some, thank you.'

What is the relationship between A and B?
questions.explanation: 'Would you like' + polite response = friendly relationship.

questions.questionText:
Read:

Bus fare is RM 2. Train fare is RM 5. Taxi fare is RM 15.

Which is the cheapest?
questions.explanation: Bus = RM 2 (cheapest). Train = RM 5. Taxi = RM 15.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The boy walked through the dark forest. He was scared but kept going. Finally, he saw a light in the distance.

What is the boy's attitude?
questions.explanation: 'Scared but kept going' = brave and determined.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct word: 'The teacher gave the books to ___ students.'
questions.explanation: Object pronoun 'us' (object of preposition 'to'). 'We' = subject. 'Our/ours' = possessive.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct word: 'I wanted to go to the park, ___ it was raining.'
questions.explanation: 'But' = contrast (I wanted to go, BUT it rained). 'Because' = cause. 'So' = result. 'And' = addition.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct word: 'The movie was so ___ that I fell asleep.'
questions.explanation: Context 'fell asleep' = boring (opposite of exciting). Test logic.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct word: 'The cat is hiding ___ the table.'
questions.explanation: 'Hiding' = not visible = below = under. 'Under the table' = below the table.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct word: 'She ___ in this school for five years.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect (has taught) for action that started in past and continues to present.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: 'The ___ of the village was concerned about the flood.'
questions.explanation: Noun 'population' (the people living in an area). 'Populate' = verb. 'Populating' = present participle.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: 'The film was very ___ . I cried at the end.'
questions.explanation: Adjective 'moving' = causing emotion. 'Moved' = past participle (also adjective but different meaning). 'Move' = verb.

questions.questionText: Choose the most formal rewrite: 'Hey, can you help me?'

options.label: B
options.text: Excuse me, could you please assist me?

questions.explanation: 'Excuse me, could you please assist me?' is the most polite and formal version.

questions.questionText: Identify the error: 'The group of students are studying in the library.'

options.label: B
options.text: group of students are → group of students is

options.label: D
options.text: in the library → at the library

questions.explanation: Subject is 'group' (singular). Verb should be 'is', not 'are'. Subject-verb agreement error.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the apostrophe to show possession?
questions.explanation: Singular possessive = dog's. 'The dog's tail' = the tail of the dog.

questions.questionText: Combine the sentences using a conjunction: 'Ali is tall. Ali is not strong.'

options.label: B
options.text: Ali is tall but not strong.

questions.explanation: Two contrasting statements joined with 'but'. 'Tall but not strong.'

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence with the SAME meaning: 'It is difficult to find a good job these days.'

options.label: A
options.text: Finding a good job is easy.

options.label: B
options.text: Finding a good job is difficult.

options.label: C
options.text: A good job is not difficult.

questions.explanation: 'It is difficult to find' = 'Finding is difficult' (gerund form).

questions.questionText: Choose the best email subject for writing to your teacher about a missed assignment:
questions.explanation: Professional email subject should be clear, specific, and polite. 'Request for Extension - Mathematics Assignment' is most appropriate.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct greeting for a formal letter:
questions.explanation: 'Dear Sir' is formal. 'Hey buddy', 'Hi there', 'Yo' are informal.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct closing for a formal letter:
questions.explanation: 'Yours faithfully' is formal closing. 'Bye', 'See ya', 'Later' are informal.

questions.questionText: Choose the most polite way to ask for help:

options.label: C
options.text: Could you please pass me that book?

questions.explanation: 'Could you please...' is polite request form. Imperatives ('Give me!') are rude.

questions.questionText: Choose the best response: 'Excuse me, how do I get to the bank?'

options.label: B
options.text: Walk down this road for two blocks. The bank is on your left.

questions.explanation: Polite, helpful directions response.

questions.questionText: Choose the most appropriate sentence for ordering food:

options.label: B
options.text: Could I have the chicken rice, please?

questions.explanation: 'Could I have...please' is polite restaurant language.

questions.questionText: You call your friend but they don't answer. Choose the most appropriate message:

options.label: A
options.text: Hey, it's me. Call me back.

options.label: B
options.text: Hello, this is [your name]. May I leave a message? Please ask [friend's name] to call me back at [number]. Thank you.

questions.explanation: Formal telephone message format includes: greeting, identification, request, name, contact info, thanks.

questions.questionText: Choose the most appropriate apology for being late:

options.label: B
options.text: I'm so sorry I'm late. The bus was delayed.

questions.explanation: Sincere apology + brief reason. Other options are rude or deflecting blame.

questions.questionText: Choose the most appropriate invitation:

options.label: A
options.text: Come to my party or else.

options.label: C
options.text: We would be honoured by your presence at our annual dinner on [date].

questions.explanation: Formal invitation = polite, specific, formal language.

questions.questionText: Choose the most appropriate thank you message for a teacher who helped you:

options.label: C
options.text: Thank you very much for your help. I really appreciate the time you spent explaining the topic to me.

questions.explanation: Formal thank you = specific acknowledgement + appreciation.

questions.questionText: Choose the most appropriate complaint to a restaurant:

options.label: B
options.text: Excuse me, I ordered the chicken, but this is fish. Could you please correct this?

questions.explanation: Polite complaint = specific issue + clear request. No insults.

questions.questionText: Choose the most polite way to ask for clarification:

options.label: C
options.text: Sorry, could you explain that again, please?

questions.explanation: Polite clarification request = apology + request + please.

questions.questionText: Choose the most appropriate way to make a doctor's appointment by phone:

options.label: A
options.text: I need to see a doctor.

options.label: B
options.text: Hello, I'd like to make an appointment with Dr. Lee, please. Is tomorrow at 10 AM available?

options.label: D
options.text: When can I see the doctor?

questions.explanation: Polite appointment booking = greeting + clear request + specific time.

questions.questionText: Choose the most important information for a school notice about a sports day cancellation:

options.label: B
options.text: The sports day scheduled for [date] has been cancelled due to bad weather. Please collect your registration forms from the office. - Sports Department

questions.explanation: Notice format: what (cancelled), when (date), why (weather), action needed (collect forms), by whom.

questions.questionText: What does 'a piece of cake' mean?
questions.explanation: Idiom 'piece of cake' = very easy. 'The exam was a piece of cake' = the exam was very easy.

questions.questionText: What does 'It's raining cats and dogs' mean?
questions.explanation: Idiom 'raining cats and dogs' = raining heavily.

questions.questionText: When someone says 'Break a leg!' before a performance, what do they mean?
questions.explanation: Idiom 'Break a leg' = good luck (used before performances).

questions.questionText: What does 'hit the books' mean?
questions.explanation: Idiom 'hit the books' = study intensively.

questions.questionText: Choose the most polite sentence:

options.label: C
options.text: Would you mind opening the window?

questions.explanation: 'Would you mind...' = most polite. 'Please' = polite. Imperative = rude.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is most appropriate for a job interview?

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, I believe I have the relevant skills and experience for this position.

questions.explanation: Job interview = formal register. Other options are informal/slang.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct discourse marker: 'She studied hard. ___, she still failed the test.'
questions.explanation: 'However' = contrast (studied hard, BUT still failed). 'Because' = cause. 'So' = result. 'And' = addition.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct discourse marker: 'It rained heavily. ___, the match was postponed.'
questions.explanation: 'Therefore' = result (rained heavily, SO match postponed). 'However/but' = contrast. 'Although' = concession.

questions.questionText: Identify the tone: 'Dear valued customer, we regret to inform you that your subscription has expired.'
questions.explanation: Words like 'Dear valued customer', 'regret to inform' = formal business tone.

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence with correct comma use:

options.label: A
options.text: I bought apples oranges and bananas.

options.label: B
options.text: I bought apples, oranges, and bananas.

options.label: C
options.text: I bought apples oranges, and bananas.

options.label: D
options.text: I bought, apples oranges and bananas.

questions.explanation: Use commas to separate items in a list (Oxford comma optional but standard).

questions.questionText: Choose the correct contraction:
questions.explanation: 'Don't' = correct contraction (do + not). 'Dont' is missing apostrophe.

questions.questionText: Choose the most precise word: 'The doctor ___ the patient's broken arm.'
questions.explanation: 'Set' (a bone) is the most precise medical term. 'Fixed/mended' too general. 'Treated' is too vague for a broken bone.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that has a similar meaning to 'abundant'.
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities. 'Plentiful' is the closest synonym.

questions.questionText: What does the expression 'under the weather' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Under the weather' is an idiom meaning to feel slightly ill.

questions.questionText: From the sentence: 'The arid desert received no rain for years.' What does 'arid' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Arid' means having little or no rain. The context 'no rain for years' confirms this.

questions.questionText: The word 'sunflower' is formed by combining which two words?
questions.explanation: 'Sunflower' is a compound noun combining 'sun' and 'flower'.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the word 'affect' correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: The rain will affect our picnic plans.

options.label: B
options.text: The affect of the medicine was positive.

options.label: C
options.text: She felt a deep affect for her friend.

options.label: D
options.text: Affect is a type of fruit.

questions.explanation: 'Affect' (verb) means to influence something. 'Effect' (noun) means a result.

questions.questionText: What does the word 'fragile' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Fragile' means easily broken or damaged.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that best completes: 'The scientist's _____ discovery changed our understanding of genetics.'
questions.explanation: 'Epoch-making' means highly significant or revolutionary. The other options mean unimportant.

questions.questionText: Which word commonly collocates with 'pay'?
questions.explanation: 'Pay attention' is a common collocation. 'Pay money' is also valid but 'pay attention' is more idiomatic here.

questions.questionText: What does 'put off' mean in this sentence: 'Don't put off your homework.'
questions.explanation: 'Put off' means to postpone or delay something.

questions.questionText: What does 'spill the beans' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Spill the beans' means to reveal a secret.

questions.questionText: Choose the word that does NOT belong to the same word family as 'beauty'.
questions.explanation: 'Behave' is not related to 'beauty'. The others all share the same root word.

questions.questionText: What is the correct plural of 'child'?
questions.explanation: 'Child' is an irregular noun; its plural form is 'children'.

questions.questionText: Which word has a meaning closest to 'reluctant'?
questions.explanation: 'Reluctant' means unwilling or hesitant. 'Hesitant' is the closest synonym.

questions.questionText: What does 'tiny' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Tiny' means very small.

questions.questionText: The word 'telephone' comes from Greek roots meaning:
questions.explanation: 'Tele-' means 'distant' and '-phone' means 'sound/voice' in Greek.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: 'She arrived _____ the airport at noon.'
questions.explanation: We use 'at' for specific locations like airports, stations, and points.

questions.questionText: Choose the word with a similar meaning to 'brave'.
questions.explanation: 'Brave' means showing courage. 'Courageous' is the closest synonym.

questions.questionText: What does 'purchase' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Purchase' means to buy something.

questions.questionText: In which sentence is 'flower' used as a verb?

options.label: B
options.text: The plant will flower in spring.

questions.explanation: In sentence B, 'flower' is used as a verb meaning to bloom.

questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'costs an arm and a leg' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Costs an arm and a leg' is an idiom meaning very expensive.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: 'She _____ to school every day.'
questions.explanation: In the present simple, third-person singular subjects take 'goes'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct past tense: 'They _____ a movie last night.'
questions.explanation: Regular verbs take '-ed' in the past simple. 'Watch' → 'watched'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct article: 'She is _____ honest teacher.'
questions.explanation: We use 'an' before words beginning with a vowel SOUND. 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: 'The meeting is _____ Monday.'
questions.explanation: We use 'on' with specific days and dates.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct verb: 'The list of items _____ on the table.'
questions.explanation: The subject is 'list' (singular), not 'items'. Use 'is'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct reported speech: Direct: 'I am happy.' She said that she _____ happy.

questions.questionText: Choose the most appropriate apology email opening:

options.label: C
options.text: I am writing to apologize for the error in our recent shipment.

questions.explanation: Formal apology emails state the purpose clearly.

questions.questionText: What is the most appropriate way to leave a voice message for a client?

options.label: C
options.text: Hello, this is [Name] from [Company]. Please call me back at [number].

questions.explanation: Professional voicemails include name, company, and contact.

questions.questionText: Pick the most polite way to ask a colleague for help:

options.label: C
options.text: Would you mind helping me with this task when you have time?

questions.explanation: 'Would you mind' is a polite conditional request structure.

questions.questionText: Choose the most professional way to give critical feedback to a colleague:

options.label: C
options.text: I have some suggestions that could improve this report.

questions.explanation: Constructive feedback uses 'suggestions' and frames positively.

questions.questionText: Pick the most appropriate introduction at a conference:

options.label: C
options.text: Good morning. I'm Sam Wilson, a senior researcher at XYZ Labs.

questions.explanation: Conference introductions include name, role, and affiliation.

questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'on cloud nine' mean?
questions.explanation: 'On cloud nine' means feeling extremely happy or elated.

questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'speak of the devil' mean?

options.label: B
options.text: said when a person just mentioned appears

questions.explanation: 'Speak of the devil' is said when the person just mentioned arrives.

questions.questionText: What does the proverb 'practice makes perfect' mean?
questions.explanation: This proverb means regular practice leads to mastery.

questions.questionText: Pick the most polite way to decline an invitation:

options.label: C
options.text: Thank you for the invitation, but I have a prior commitment.

questions.explanation: Polite refusals thank the inviter and provide a reason.

questions.questionText: Your roommate says 'It's getting late, isn't it?' What do they probably want?
questions.explanation: This is an indirect suggestion. The speaker wants to leave.

questions.questionText: Which action do you do every morning before going to school?
questions.explanation: Brushing your teeth is one of the daily morning actions you do before going to school. It is part of a healthy daily routine.

questions.questionText: Look outside. Dark clouds and strong winds are blowing. What word describes this weather?
questions.explanation: Dark clouds and strong winds describe stormy weather.

questions.questionText: Your friend looks sad. What word describes how they feel?
questions.explanation: Looking sad is being upset. 'Upset' means feeling unhappy.

questions.questionText: Your mother's mother is your _______.
questions.explanation: Your mother's mother is your grandmother.

questions.questionText: Which one is a healthy snack?
questions.explanation: An apple is a healthy snack. Chips and sweets are unhealthy.

questions.questionText: It is 12 o'clock in the middle of the day. What is this time called?
questions.explanation: 12 o'clock in the daytime is called noon.

questions.questionText: Which item do you use to carry your books to school?
questions.explanation: A backpack is used to carry books and items to school.

questions.questionText: You want to travel across the sea to an island. Which transport should you take?
questions.explanation: A ship travels across the sea to islands.

questions.questionText: Which adjective describes the weather when there are no clouds in the sky?
questions.explanation: No clouds in the sky means sunny weather.

questions.questionText: Which body part do you use to hear sounds?
questions.explanation: You use your ears to hear sounds.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: She go to school every day.

options.label: B
options.text: She goes to school every day.

options.label: C
options.text: She going to school every day.

options.label: D
options.text: She gone to school every day.

questions.explanation: With 'she/he/it', we add -s to the verb: 'goes'.

questions.questionText: Read this situation: A boy is kicking a ball. Which sentence is correct?

options.label: B
options.text: The boy is kicking a ball.

options.label: D
options.text: The boy kicks a ball yesterday.

questions.explanation: Present continuous: subject + is/are + verb-ing. 'The boy is kicking a ball.'

questions.questionText: Yesterday, I ____ to the market with my mother.
questions.explanation: Past simple of 'go' is 'went'. 'I went to the market yesterday.'

questions.questionText: The cat is hiding ____ the table. We cannot see it.
questions.explanation: When something is below and hidden, we use 'under'.

questions.questionText: I saw ____ elephant at the zoo. ____ elephant was very big.
questions.explanation: 'An' before words starting with vowel sound (elephant). 'The' for specific things we already mentioned.

questions.questionText: The teacher asked Ahmad and ____ to come to the staff room.
questions.explanation: After a verb, use object pronoun 'him'. 'The teacher asked Ahmad and him to come.'

questions.questionText: Which word is the correct plural form of 'child'?
questions.explanation: The plural of 'child' is 'children' (irregular plural).

questions.questionText: My brother is ____ than me. He is taller.
questions.explanation: Comparative of 'tall' is 'taller' (compares two things).

questions.questionText: Mount Kinabalu is the ____ mountain in Malaysia.
questions.explanation: Superlative of 'tall' is 'tallest' (compares three or more).

questions.questionText: I ____ swim. I learnt it when I was 5 years old.
questions.explanation: Modal verb 'can' does not change form. 'I can swim.'

questions.questionText: I like mangoes ____ I do not like durian. They smell too strong.
questions.explanation: 'But' shows contrast. 'I like mangoes but I do not like durian.'

questions.questionText: Your friend is at the cinema and you want to know when the movie begins. You ask: '____ does the movie begin?'
questions.explanation: 'When' asks about time. 'Where' asks about place, 'Why' asks about reason, 'Who' asks about people.

questions.questionText:
Read:

Sara walks to school every morning. On her way, she passes a small park. In the park, there are many colourful flowers. Sara always stops to look at them.

What does Sara see in the park?
questions.explanation: The petikan says 'there are many colourful flowers.'

questions.questionText:
Read:

Yesterday, Ali and his father went to the library. Ali borrowed three books. His father read a newspaper. They stayed there for one hour.

Who went to the library with Ali?
questions.explanation: The petikan says 'Ali and his father went to the library.'

questions.questionText:
Read:

Last weekend, my family went to Penang. We visited the beach and ate delicious food. We took many photos and had a great time together.

Where did the family go?
questions.explanation: The petikan says 'my family went to Penang.'

questions.questionText:
Read:

Aisha looked out of the window. The sky was dark and she heard thunder. She quickly closed all the windows and took her cat inside.

Why did Aisha close the windows?

options.label: C
options.text: She thought there would be a storm.

questions.explanation: Dark sky and thunder suggest a coming storm. Aisha closed the windows to protect her home.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The little kitten had soft white fur and bright blue eyes. It loved to play with a red ball of yarn. When it was tired, it would curl up on a warm blanket by the window.

What is the colour of the kitten's eyes?
questions.explanation: The petikan says 'bright blue eyes.'

questions.questionText:
Read:

First, wash the apple. Next, cut it into small pieces. Then, put the pieces into a bowl. Finally, add some honey and mix well.

What do you do AFTER cutting the apple?

options.label: C
options.text: Put the pieces into a bowl

questions.explanation: The sequence says: wash → cut → put into bowl → add honey. So after cutting, you put pieces into a bowl.

questions.questionText:
Read:

Teacher: 'Have you finished your homework?'
Student: 'I tried, but I did not understand question 5.'

What can we infer about the student?

options.label: B
options.text: The student has difficulty with the homework.

options.label: C
options.text: The student forgot to bring the homework.

options.label: D
options.text: The student is the teacher's pet.

questions.explanation: The student said they 'did not understand' question 5, showing difficulty with the work.

questions.questionText:
Read:

Many children in rural areas have to walk a long way to reach school. Some walk through forests, cross rivers, or climb hills. Despite the difficulty, they go to school every day to learn and achieve their dreams.

What is the main idea of this petikan?

options.label: B
options.text: Children in rural areas face challenges to go to school.

options.label: C
options.text: There are many forests in Malaysia.

questions.explanation: The petikan describes the challenges rural children face to attend school.

questions.questionText:
Read:

The old man walked slowly with a walking stick. His back was bent and his hair was white. He stopped often to rest and catch his breath.

How old is the man likely to be?
questions.explanation: Walking slowly, bent back, white hair and needing rest suggest he is elderly.

questions.questionText:
Read:

GRAND SALE! Up to 50% off all items. This weekend only at MegaMart, Lot 12. Open from 10am to 9pm. Free gift for the first 100 customers! Where is the sale?
questions.explanation: The advertisement says 'at MegaMart, Lot 12.'

questions.questionText: Complete the sentence: 'If it rains tomorrow, we ____ at home.'
questions.explanation: First conditional: 'If + present, will + verb'. 'We will stay at home.'

questions.questionText: She is the girl ____ won the singing competition.
questions.explanation: For people, use 'who'. 'She is the girl who won.'

questions.questionText: Which sentence has the correct word order?

options.label: A
options.text: I every day go to school.

options.label: B
options.text: I go every day to school.

options.label: C
options.text: I go to school every day.

options.label: D
options.text: Go I to school every day.

questions.explanation: Standard English word order: Subject + Verb + Object + Adverb of frequency. 'I go to school every day.'

questions.questionText: Which sentence has a grammar error?
questions.explanation: With 'he/she/it', we use 'doesn't'. 'He doesn't like durian.'

questions.questionText: Which sentence is most suitable for a formal letter to your principal?

options.label: A
options.text: Hey, can you let me off early today?

options.label: B
options.text: Dear Sir, I would like to request a half-day leave.

options.label: C
options.text: Yo! Need to go home. Thanks.

questions.explanation: Formal letters use respectful salutations and polite language. 'Dear Sir, I would like to request...' is appropriate.

questions.questionText: Combine these two sentences into ONE good sentence: 'The boy is tall. He plays basketball.'

options.label: A
options.text: The boy is tall plays basketball.

questions.explanation: Move the adjective 'tall' before the noun 'boy' to combine the sentences naturally.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is the clearest way to invite a friend to your birthday party?

options.label: B
options.text: Come to my birthday party at my house on Saturday.

questions.explanation: A clear invitation includes: event, location, and time. 'Come to my birthday party at my house on Saturday.' covers all.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses punctuation correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: Where are you going, asked Sara.

options.label: B
options.text: Where are you going? asked Sara.

options.label: C
options.text: Where are you going. Asked Sara.

options.label: D
options.text: Where are you going, asked Sara

questions.explanation: Direct questions use '?'. After the question, capitalize the new sentence. 'Where are you going? asked Sara.'

questions.questionText: You are at a job interview. Which sentence is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Yeah, I can do that stuff, no worries.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, I am confident I can manage that task well.

questions.explanation: Job interviews require polite, formal language. Option B is professional and appropriate.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is the most polite way to ask your teacher for help?

options.label: C
options.text: Excuse me, Sir. Could you please help me with this question?

questions.explanation: Polite requests use: 'Excuse me', title (Sir/Madam), modal verb (could/would), and 'please'.

questions.questionText: Your friend says: 'It's raining cats and dogs!' What does this mean?

options.label: A
options.text: Animals are falling from the sky.

options.label: C
options.text: There are cats and dogs in the rain.

questions.explanation: 'Raining cats and dogs' is an idiom meaning it is raining very heavily.

questions.questionText: Which word best completes: 'I was walking home. ____, I saw a dog.'
questions.explanation: 'Suddenly' shows an unexpected event happening in the moment. 'Suddenly, I saw a dog.'

questions.questionText: What does 'look after' mean? 'I look after my little brother.'
questions.explanation: Phrasal verb 'look after' means 'to take care of'. 'I take care of my little brother.'

questions.questionText: You need to leave a note for your mother saying you have gone to the library. Which is best?

options.label: B
options.text: Dear Mum, I have gone to the library. Back by 5pm. - Love, Aini

questions.explanation: A good note includes: greeting, the message clearly stated, time/expected return, and sign-off.

questions.questionText: You are lost and want to find the post office. Which sentence is most appropriate to ask a stranger?

options.label: C
options.text: Excuse me, could you please tell me the way to the post office?

questions.explanation: Polite directions request: 'Excuse me', modal verb (could/would), 'please', and a clear question.

questions.questionText: You are at a restaurant. Which sentence is the correct way to order?

options.label: C
options.text: Could I please have a chicken rice?

questions.explanation: Polite orders use: modal verb (could), 'please', and a clear request.

questions.questionText: Someone calls your house. You answer the phone. What is the correct way to greet?

options.label: C
options.text: Hello, this is the Lee residence.

questions.explanation: Telephone greetings are formal: 'Hello, this is [name] speaking' or 'this is the [family] residence'.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is most suitable for an email to your teacher?

options.label: A
options.text: Yo teacher, I didn't do the homework lol.

options.label: B
options.text: Dear Sir, I am writing to inform you that I was unable to submit my homework due to illness. Thank you for your understanding.

questions.explanation: Formal emails use: respectful salutation (Dear Sir/Madam), polite language, clear explanation, and gratitude.
